name: Prologis, Inc.

profile.description: Prologis, Inc. is the world's largest industrial/logistics REIT, with roughly $238B of gross assets under management serving e-commerce, retail, manufacturing and third-party logistics customers, plus growing data center and energy businesses [1][2]. CEO Dan Letter, who succeeded co-founder Hamid Moghadam in January 2026, is pursuing an 'intelligent infrastructure' strategy that includes a 5.8 GW secured or advanced-stage power pipeline for data centers and an ~$18.8B recommended all-share acquisition of UK-listed SEGRO plc, expected to close in 2027 [2][3][4]. Q3 2026 revenue was $2.39B (+7.8% YoY) with Core FFO of $1.60 per share versus $1.49 a year earlier [1].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Prologis has transformed itself multiple times in five years — the Duke Realty merger lifted annual revenue from $4.76B (2021) to $8.02B (2023) [9], the company built a data center development business now backed by a 5.8 GW power pipeline [2], and in August 2026 it agreed to acquire SEGRO for ~$18.8B in stock to consolidate UK/European logistics [3]. AI Deployment (1/2): Prologis is converting warehouses into turnkey data centers (e.g., an Illinois conversion and a Chicago development sold to HMC Capital) and funds AI, robotics and supply-chain technology through Prologis Ventures, but it has not quantified internal AI savings or AI revenue in its disclosures [4][11]. Market Share (2/2): With ~$238B gross AUM, 95.5% occupancy and 60M sq ft leased in Q3 2026 alone, Prologis is the category-defining global logistics landlord [2]. Pipeline (2/2): 2026 development-start guidance was raised to $6.0–6.75B, Q3 starts were $964M at a 6.6% estimated yield, and management plans ~$8B for 20 data center projects over four years [1][2][4]. R&D (0/1): As a REIT, Prologis reports no R&D expense [9].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Prologis describes itself as creating 'the intelligent infrastructure that powers global commerce, seamlessly connecting the digital and physical worlds' — a specific, thoughtful purpose that has visibly driven strategy into data centers and clean energy, though it has not yet been validated over decades the way a 4 requires [8][4]. Community Impact (2/2): The company runs an annual global IMPACT Day volunteer program across its markets and pairs it with community workforce initiatives; its 2026 proxy cites an ISS ESG 'Prime' rating and an MSCI 'AA' rating, and Sustainalytics rates its ESG risk management as strong [10][6][7]. Employee Retention (1/2): New CEO Dan Letter worked alongside Moghadam for more than 20 years before an orderly internal succession, signaling leadership continuity, but Prologis does not publish turnover or tenure figures [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by executives was found in the trailing 12 months.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 10 dividend-sleeve metrics (weighted sum 10.17 of 12). Strengths: D/E of 62% is under the 70% target, 5-yr revenue CAGR is 14.6% (FY2020 $4.44B to FY2025 $8.79B, computed from reported statements), TTM profit margin is 43% (lifted by $784M of 9-month disposition gains), the dividend has been paid 29 straight years with 13 consecutive annual increases, and the 5-yr dividend CAGR is 11.7% ($2.32 in 2020 to $4.04 in 2025) [8][9][2]. Drags: ROE of 7.7% (0.51), forward P/E of 35.6 (0.61) and a GAAP payout ratio of 93% (0.12) — the latter two reflect REIT depreciation, since Core FFO guidance of $6.25–6.29 covers the $4.28 annual dividend comfortably [1][8]. Q3 2026 revenue growth of 7.8% scores 0.93; debt/EBITDA is 4.5x with $8.8B of liquidity at a 3.3% average borrowing cost [1][2].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Prologis owns physical logistics real estate — warehouses that store and move goods at 95.5% occupancy — which AI cannot substitute; no analyst coverage found frames AI as a threat to its core warehouse business [2][4]. AI instead adds demand: management says data centers are one of the largest value-creation opportunities in company history, with a 5.8 GW secured/advanced power pipeline and plans for ~$8B across 20 projects [2][4]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Prologis is already monetizing AI-driven demand by delivering and selling powered data center projects, such as the Chicago data center development sold to HMC Capital and a converted Illinois warehouse delivered as a turnkey data center [4][11].

infinite_game.summary: Prologis behaves like a long-horizon steward of global logistics infrastructure: it survived the 2008–09 crisis by cutting its dividend from $2.00 to $1.12 and rebuilding to 12 straight years of increases, executed a planned founder-to-insider CEO succession, and is now extending its purpose into data centers and energy [5][8]. Sinek would credit its consistency and courage, but its 'we don't just lead the industry, we define it' self-description and its pursuit of SEGRO after the target's board 'unequivocally rejected' the first approach read as a finite, dominance-oriented competitive posture [3][8].

just_cause.analysis: Prologis's cause — intelligent infrastructure that powers global commerce and connects the digital and physical worlds — is distinctive and clearly shapes decisions such as the data center and energy build-outs [8][4]. It is a genuine cause partially lived, but it is framed around the company's own leadership position rather than a future state others sacrifice to advance, so it falls short of a full Just Cause (2/3).

trusting_teams.analysis: The organization is stable: Dan Letter rose internally after more than 20 years working with co-founder Moghadam, and the 2024 shareholder letter describes his style as rooted in collaboration and innovation [5]. No published turnover, tenure or culture data distinguishes Prologis as an exceptional high-trust workplace (1/2).

worthy_rivals.analysis: Prologis's own messaging says it doesn't 'just lead the industry, they define it,' and it pressed on with SEGRO — raising its exchange ratio 9.5% after the board rejected the initial £12.6B approach — a consolidation-oriented stance rather than learning from rivals [3][8]. No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors as benchmarks for self-improvement (0/1).

existential_flexibility.analysis: Prologis is redefining what a logistics REIT is — converting urban warehouses into data centers, building a multi-gigawatt power pipeline, and adding energy and venture businesses under an 'intelligent infrastructure' identity [2][4][11]. This is a deliberate, purpose-driven reinvention from pure warehouse landlord toward digital infrastructure, undertaken from a position of strength (2/2).

courage_to_lead.analysis: Leadership has repeatedly chosen long-term capability over near-term optics: it cut the dividend from $2.00 (2007) to $1.12 (2009) to protect the balance sheet, then rebuilt it to $4.04 by 2025 [8]. It is now committing ~$8B to data centers and raised 2026 development starts to $6.0–6.75B even as GAAP EPS guidance was cut to $4.05–4.15 (2/2) [1][4].

investment_thesis: Prologis is the dominant global logistics landlord compounding cash flow: Q3 2026 Core FFO rose to $1.60 from $1.49 (beating the $1.56 consensus), occupancy held at 95.5%, 60M sq ft were leased, and cash same-store NOI guidance was raised to 7.0–7.5% [1][2]. On top of the core, a 5.8 GW data center power pipeline and the ~$18.8B SEGRO acquisition (which SEGRO shareholders have approved, with A2/A ratings expected to be maintained) extend its scale and position it to capture AI-driven infrastructure demand, while 4.5x debt/EBITDA and a 3.3% average cost of debt keep the balance sheet conservative [2][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and execution: the stock trades at 35.6x forward GAAP earnings (~20x Core FFO) and the GAAP payout ratio is 93% [8][1]. GAAP EPS guidance was cut to $4.05–4.15 from $4.40–4.55 because earnings lean on lumpy disposition gains, Q3 rental revenue of $2.22B reportedly missed estimates, and integrating SEGRO in an all-share deal dilutes existing holders and adds UK/European exposure into 2027 [1][2][3]. Data center development brings power-procurement, tenant-concentration and capital-intensity risks outside Prologis's historic core competency.
key_catalysts: Closing of the ~$18.8B SEGRO acquisition (targeted 2027) adds a large UK/European urban logistics and data center portfolio with expected cost and development synergies while maintaining A2/A credit ratings [3]
Monetization of the 5.8 GW data center power pipeline — management targets ~$8B across 20 projects over four years, with sales or leases to hyperscalers crystallizing value [2][4]
Raised 2026 development starts guidance ($6.0–6.75B) at ~6.6% yields plus 7.0–7.5% cash same-store NOI growth support continued Core FFO and dividend growth [1][2]
key_risks: SEGRO integration and share dilution: the all-share consideration (0.0920 PLD shares per SEGRO share) and partial cash alternative raise execution risk and FX exposure through a 2027 close [3]
GAAP earnings volatility — 2026 net earnings guidance was cut to $4.05–4.15 because results depend on lumpy disposition gains, keeping the GAAP payout ratio near 93% [1][2]
Data center development requires securing scarce power and long-dated hyperscaler commitments; delays or a pullback in AI capex would strand capital in a newer, less proven business line [4]
